the GABA receptor-chloride channel complex in the HAS rats is more sensitive to the inhibitory effects of barbiturates, benzodiazepines, and ethanol than the GABA receptor in LAS rats.

the high alcohol sensitivity lines are more sensitive to the sedative effects of pentobarbitol, phenobarbittol, flunitrazepan and ethanol on GABAA receptors than the low alcohol sensitivity line, and that the high alcohol lines have more GABAA receptors that bind diazepam than the low alcohol lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model system to study the genetic basis of alcohol sensitivity.
the role of the GABA receptor-chloride channel complex in the acute behavioral effects of alcohol and other sedative hypnotic drugs.
the genetic and neurobiological bases of individual differences in sensitivity to the effects of alcohol and other drugs of abuse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HAS rats are more sensitive to GABAergic agents than LAS rats, but the mechanism for this increased sensitivity remains to be determined.

these lines of selectively bred rats do not differ in the GABA receptor-chloride channel complex but do differ in the benzodiazepine receptor-GABA receptor-chlorine channel complex, and these differences appear to be related to the lines' differential response to the sedative hypnotic drugs.
the differences observed between the HAS and LAS lines in the present study are not related to GABA receptor function, but are related to some other aspect of GABAergic function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
differences between the lines are observed in response to various sedative hypnotics and not in GABA-mediated chloride channel function.
the HAS rats are more sensitive to the sedative effects of GABA-ergic agents and that this may be due, at least in part, to a greater number of GABA receptors in these rats.
the differences between the lines are not due to differences in the number of receptors or in the intrinsic affinity of the receptor, but are due to differences in post-receptor mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
differences exist between the lines in the modulation of GABAergic function by various sedative hypnotics.
the HAS and LAS lines display differences in the modulation of the chloride channel, but not in the GABA receptor itself.
